answers:
I found 21 problems across the three new files. The biggest one: the new endpoint never goes live, because `app/main.py` doesn't import `loyalty_routes`.

## `app/api/loyalty_routes.py`

1. **`app/main.py:1-3`**: `loyalty_routes` is missing from the import list that registers routes, so `GET /customers/{id}/loyalty` returns 404 and `LoyaltyBadge` never gets data.
2. **`loyalty_routes.py:10`**: It reads `os.environ` directly. The rest of the app uses `app/config.py` `Settings`, so add `loyalty_rate` there. Because the value is parsed on every request, a bad `LOYALTY_RATE` value causes a `ValueError` and a 500 on each call instead of failing once at startup.
3. **`loyalty_routes.py:11`**: The route queries the database itself instead of going through a service. `customer_service.get_customer` already exists, and so does `loyalty_service.find_customer`, which isn't used here.
4. **`loyalty_routes.py:12-13`**: An unknown customer gets a 200 with `{"points": 0}`, which looks the same as a real customer with zero points. `show_customer` raises `LookupError` for a missing customer, and this route should behave the same way.
5. **`loyalty_routes.py:14-15`**: The tier rule (gold doubles the rate) sits in the HTTP layer, while `points_for` adds its own gold bonus at `loyalty_service.py:16`. Gold logic is split across two files, which makes it easy to double-count or change only one place. Move it all into the service.

## `app/services/loyalty_service.py`

6. **`:1`**: `import json` is never used.
7. **`:6-10`**: `find_customer` is dead code. The `if row is None: return None; return row` part also does nothing; it's the same as `return db.fetch_one(...)`. And it repeats `customer_service.get_customer`.
8. **`:13`**: It takes an untyped `dict` instead of the `Customer` model. It reads fields the model doesn't have (`spent_cents`, `referrals`, `birthday_month`, `newsletter`, `blocked`). Either the schema and model disagree, or `.get()` quietly returns defaults for columns that don't exist.
9. **`:14`, `:24`, `:26`**: The `.get(key, 0)` defaults don't protect you. `fetch_one` returns every column, so the key exists with value `None` when the column is NULL. Then `spent * rate` and `None > 3` raise `TypeError`. Use `customer.get("x") or 0`.
10. **`:15-33`**: Unnamed numbers are everywhere (`100`, `50/20/5`, `10`, `3`, `25`, `5`, `3`, `1000`). Name them as constants.
11. **`:16-21`**: The `if/elif` chain calls `customer.get("tier")` three times. A `TIER_BONUS = {"gold": 50, ...}` lookup would be simpler.
12. **`:24-27`**: `customer.get("referrals", 0)` is evaluated twice. Read it into a variable once.
13. **`:30-31`**: The `blocked` check runs after all the points are added up and then sets them to zero. Return early at the top instead.
14. **`:32-33`**: Gold customers are exempt from the 1000-point cap. That's a business rule with no comment or name explaining it.
15. **(no file)**: There are no tests for `points_for`, even though it has many branches.

## `web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx`

16. **`:6`**: It uses raw `fetch` with a hard-coded `/api` prefix instead of `apiClient` from `lib/apiClient.ts`. Other features put their calls in a `web/src/api/*.ts` module, so this should get a `web/src/api/loyalty.ts` with a typed response.
17. **`:7-8`**: There's no `response.ok` check and no `.catch`. A 404 or 500 body sets `points` to `undefined`, so the badge shows "undefined pts", and network errors become unhandled promise rejections.
18. **`:4`, `:11`**: There's no loading state. The badge shows "0 pts" before the data arrives, which looks like a real value.
19. **`:5-9`**: The effect has no cleanup or `AbortController`. If `customerId` changes, a slower old response can overwrite the new one.
20. **`:10`**: A `debugger;` statement is left in the render function, so it pauses on every render whenever devtools are open.
21. **`:14-25`**: `summarize` has nothing to do with the badge and isn't used anywhere. It's also the third copy of the same function (see `OrderList.tsx:24` and `InvoiceList.tsx:24`); move it to `web/src/lib/` and share it. Lines 22-23 format money with `(cents / 100).toFixed(2)` instead of the existing `formatCents` in `lib/format.ts`, so the currency formatting won't match the rest of the app. It also has no declared return type.

Unrelated to your changes, `web/src/hooks/useOrderTotals.ts` already in the repo has the same leftover `debugger;` and uses `==` where it should be `===` (the `eqeqeq` lint rule flags it).

cat app/config.py web/src/lib/apiClient.ts web/src/lib/format.ts web/src/hooks/useOrderTotals.ts app/api/customer_routes.py app/services/customer_service.py web/src/api/customer.ts .oxlintrc.json

grep -rn "summarize\|LoyaltyBadge\|loyalty" web app | grep -v "^web/src/components/LoyaltyBadge.tsx\|^app/services/loyalty_service.py\|^app/api/loyalty_routes.py"; grep -n "import\|route" app/main.py | head
